name: Katharine Bradley
bio: Poet, born 1846, the elder half of "Michael Field" and the aunt of her collaborator and life partner Edith Cooper (1862-1913), whom she raised. "Michael Field" is not a person but the single joint pen name under which Bradley and Cooper published everything: eight volumes of poetry, some twenty-seven verse dramas, and a joint diary, Works and Days. Wilde addressed his letters to "Michael Field", writing to the pair as one correspondent. Bradley and Cooper came from a well-off Birmingham family, read classics at University College, Bristol, and lived together first in Reigate and finally in Richmond; on the Y90s account Bradley was the older and the more glamorous and expansive of the two, and was "Michael" (also the Simiorg, or All-Wise-Fowl) in the private mythology of the diary. Wilde corresponded with "Michael Field" between 1890 and 1893 about their verse dramas and about placing A Question of Memory with J. T. Grein's Independent Theatre. Bradley survived Cooper by less than a year and died in 1914.
bio_note: Dates from the editors' identifying footnote to Wilde's letter to 'Michael Field', Complete Letters (2000), p. 449 (the editors print 'Katherine'; 'Katharine' follows the Y90s biography and her own usage).
